findings: Every VALIDATED rule is obeyed: harmony-clash notes 22–48% (r1–r3) → 0% on all three; register violations 0; off-16th-grid notes 0; all 10 pads used; drum clip covers all 32 beats; Opus runs one clip per track. The ear did not move. harmony_clash is now the second proxy in this project driven to zero with no verdict change (the passing r2 composition was itself flagged by it).

Opus drum grids are near-identical across seeds 1 and 2, and bar 2 repeats bar 1 in both: the prompt forbids static repetition but prescribes the jerk core so tightly the model renders it as a literal template. Both 808 lines open 62→65 from the same pitch set.

Sonnet-s3 wrote 24 clips on 9 tracks: arp had 5 overlapping clips (4 simultaneous notes on every 16th on a monophonic role); drums had 2 overlapping clips (432 hits, 304 duplicates). No validator enforces one clip per track or monophony — the two rules without validators are the two still violated.

Sound selection is seed luck: seed 3 drew the same seven Vital presets as the r3c clean pass, so sonnet-s3 failed on notes alone with approved sounds; seeds 1/2 drew different presets and both drew 'bad sound selection'. No preset in the 60-preset bank has ever been auditioned by ear.
Confound: no labkit twin this round (r2/r3c passes were all on the owner's own kit), so palette-vs-labkit and notes-vs-sounds cannot be separated from these three renders.

Owner's 'wrong notes' = pitch clash with bass/key AND register/voicing AND placement/timing. Pitch-set and register checks read zero, so what he hears lives outside every writable rule: contour, voice-leading, phrase logic, hit choice.
